title: Who Makes Them, and How Many Are Kept

scenes.tts: Adult rodents make new neurons. Which cell makes them, and how many are kept?
scenes.visual: Title card: Who Makes Them, and How Many Are Kept. A mouse brain in side view.
scenes.narration: Adult rodents make new neurons. Which cell makes them, and how many are kept?

scenes.tts: They appear in two places. One is the subventricular zone, in the wall of the lateral ventricles.
scenes.visual: The lateral ventricle wall highlighted in the mouse brain.
scenes.narration: They appear in two places. One is the subventricular zone, in the wall of the lateral ventricles.

scenes.tts: Its young neurons migrate forward in chains to the olfactory bulb.
scenes.visual: Chains of young neurons move forward along the rostral migratory stream to the olfactory bulb.
scenes.narration: Its young neurons migrate forward in chains to the olfactory bulb.

scenes.tts: The other is the dentate gyrus of the hippocampus. There, the rate falls steeply with age.
scenes.visual: The dentate gyrus highlighted. A small line falls with age; label: schematic.
scenes.narration: The other is the dentate gyrus of the hippocampus. There, the rate falls steeply with age.

scenes.tts: Four kinds of cell sit in that wall. Ependymal cells line it, with astrocyte-like B cells beneath.
scenes.visual: Cartoon of the ventricle wall: ependymal cells as a separate lining sheet with cilia; astrocyte-like cells beneath, labelled B cells.
scenes.narration: Four kinds of cell sit in that wall. Ependymal cells line it, with astrocyte-like B cells beneath.

scenes.tts: Both divide rarely. Fast-dividing C cells multiply, and young neurons, the ay cells, migrate away.
scenes.visual: Fast-dividing precursors, labelled C cells, and neuroblasts, labelled A cells, highlighted.
scenes.narration: Both divide rarely. Fast-dividing C cells multiply, and young neurons, the A cells, migrate away.
scenes.caption: Both divide rarely. Fast-dividing C cells multiply, and young neurons, the A cells, migrate away.

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-nine, Fiona Doetsch and colleagues infused adult mice with a drug that kills cells copying DNA, then stopped.
scenes.caption: In 1999, Fiona Doetsch and colleagues infused adult mice with a drug that kills cells copying DNA, then stopped.
scenes.visual: Credit card: Doetsch and colleagues, 1999, adult mouse. A drug wash flows over the zone.
scenes.narration: In 1999, Fiona Doetsch and colleagues infused adult mice with a drug that kills cells copying DNA, then stopped.

scenes.tts: Pause and predict. Which cells survive? And which one rebuilds the zone?
scenes.visual: Question card: which cells survive, and which rebuilds the zone?
scenes.narration: Pause and predict. Which cells survive? And which one rebuilds the zone?

scenes.tts: The fast dividers and most neuroblasts died. The rare dividers survived.
scenes.visual: The fast dividers and neuroblasts fade; the lining sheet and astrocyte-like cells remain.
scenes.narration: The fast dividers and most neuroblasts died. The rare dividers survived.

scenes.tts: Then the astrocyte-like cells divided. Precursors came back, then neuroblasts, in the normal order.
scenes.visual: The astrocyte-like cells light up and divide; precursors refill, then neuroblasts, in order.
scenes.narration: Then the astrocyte-like cells divided. Precursors came back, then neuroblasts, in the normal order.

scenes.tts: That makes them the leading candidate, not yet proof. Proof needs an inherited label showing the neurons descend from an astrocyte-like cell, in the same cells as neuron identity.
scenes.visual: The two-fact rule card returns briefly: an inherited label from an astrocyte-like cell, plus neuron identity, in the same cells.
scenes.narration: That makes them the leading candidate, not yet proof. Proof needs an inherited label showing the neurons descend from an astrocyte-like cell, in the same cells as neuron identity.

scenes.tts: This retrovirus writes its genes into the chromosome of a dividing cell, so every descendant inherits them.
scenes.visual: A virus inserts a gene into the chromosome of a dividing cell; the gene is passed to every daughter in a family tree.
scenes.narration: This retrovirus writes its genes into the chromosome of a dividing cell, so every descendant inherits them.

scenes.tts: This virus enters only through one receptor. The mice were engineered to make it only in cells making G F A P.
scenes.caption: This virus enters only through one receptor. The mice were engineered to make it only in cells making GFAP.
scenes.visual: Only GFAP-positive astrocyte-like cells carry the receptor; the virus docks there and nowhere else.
scenes.narration: This virus enters only through one receptor. The mice were engineered to make it only in cells making GFAP.

scenes.tts: So in untreated mice, only astrocyte-like cells were infected. Later, the marker turned up in new olfactory bulb neurons.
scenes.visual: The inherited marker is followed along the migratory stream into an olfactory bulb neuron.
scenes.narration: So in untreated mice, only astrocyte-like cells were infected. Later, the marker turned up in new olfactory bulb neurons.

scenes.tts: The dentate gyrus follows the same plan, with radial, astrocyte-like stem cells.
scenes.visual: Split screen: the dentate gyrus with a radial stem cell at the inner edge of the granule layer.
scenes.narration: The dentate gyrus follows the same plan, with radial, astrocyte-like stem cells.

scenes.tts: How many are kept? In mice, many newborn cells die early, mostly within the first days.
scenes.visual: A large share of newborn cells fade, most of the loss in the first days; the rest remain. Schematic, not counts.
scenes.narration: How many are kept? In mice, many newborn cells die early, mostly within the first days.

scenes.tts: Later, while they mature, survival also depends partly on their own activity.
scenes.visual: The surviving young neurons light up with incoming input.
scenes.narration: Later, while they mature, survival also depends partly on their own activity.

scenes.tts: Young neurons lacking N M D A receptors survive less well than their neighbours. Other survival signals may help too.
scenes.caption: Young neurons lacking NMDA receptors survive less well than their neighbours. Other survival signals may help too.
scenes.visual: One young neuron without NMDA receptors fades among labelled neighbours that keep their receptors. Credit: Tashiro and colleagues, 2006, mouse.
scenes.narration: Young neurons lacking NMDA receptors survive less well than their neighbours. Other survival signals may help too.

scenes.tts: More new neurons can mean more division, or more young cells kept. Two time points help tell them apart.
scenes.visual: A timeline: one dose, a look at one day, a look at four weeks.
scenes.narration: More new neurons can mean more division, or more young cells kept. Two time points help tell them apart.

scenes.tts: After one dose of B R D U, a one-day count is an index of division. At four weeks, label plus a neuron protein counts labelled cells that are neurons by then.
scenes.caption: After one dose of BrdU, a one-day count is an index of division. At four weeks, label plus a neuron protein counts labelled cells that are neurons by then.
scenes.visual: Two labelled boxes: one day, mostly dividing cells, an index of division; four weeks, BrdU plus NeuN, labelled cells that are neurons by then.
scenes.narration: After one dose of BrdU, a one-day count is an index of division. At four weeks, label plus a neuron protein counts labelled cells that are neurons by then.

scenes.tts: Pause and predict. If running acted only on division, what would you see at each time point?
scenes.visual: Question card: running acts only on division. One day? Four weeks?
scenes.narration: Pause and predict. If running acted only on division, what would you see at each time point?

scenes.tts: More labelled cells at one day, and more new neurons at four weeks, in the same proportion.
scenes.visual: A two-row chart: runners above controls at both time points; the late-to-early ratio equal. Labelled: predicted pattern, assumes later steps unchanged, not data.
scenes.narration: More labelled cells at one day, and more new neurons at four weeks, in the same proportion.

scenes.tts: In those mouse studies, running mainly raised division. Enriched housing mainly raised survival.
scenes.visual: Two icons: a running wheel, labelled division; a large cage with toys and companions, labelled survival.
scenes.narration: In those mouse studies, running mainly raised division. Enriched housing mainly raised survival.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: the stem cell looks glial, and born is not the same as kept.
scenes.visual: Closing card: glial-like stem cells; born is not kept.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: the stem cell looks glial, and born is not the same as kept.
